title: Article 37 — Application of the Directive Principles

content.overview: Article 37 is the key to Part IV. The provisions of Part IV are not enforceable by any court, but the principles are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws. Verify exact text against the official Constitution.

sections.heading: Non-enforceability
sections.body: Courts do not enforce Directive Principles as freestanding rights. A petition that seeks relief solely because a Directive Principle exists, without an enforceable legal right or implementing framework, is misconceived under Article 37.

sections.heading: Duty in governance and law-making
sections.body: Article 37 also states that the principles are fundamental in governance and that the State must apply them in making laws. That duty is political and constitutional in character; its justiciable edge, if any, runs through statutes, schemes, and Part III standards — not through rewriting Article 37.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Frame claims under the implementing Act or under Articles 14, 19 or 21 as applicable. Use the Directive Principle to explain policy purpose. Do not plead Part IV as a substitute for Part III.

sections.heading: Historical vs current
sections.body: HISTORICAL: early case law sometimes stressed subordination of Part IV to Part III in conflict settings. CURRENT PRACTICE: harmonisation is the preferred interpretive posture where possible, always subject to Article 37's non-enforceability rule and to controlling authority on Article 31C and basic structure.
